title: A Thing of Beauty is a Joy For Ever

topics.name: Inversion after never, seldom, rarely, not only, hardly

options: The sunset was more lovelier than the sunrise.
The sunset was lovelier than the sunrise.
The sunset was loveliest than the sunrise.
questions.rule: Comparing two things: use the comparative lovelier + than. Never add more to an -er word.

options: The daffodils which grow by the stream are yellow.
The daffodils who grow by the stream are yellow.
The daffodils which grows by the stream are yellow.
questions.rule: Use which for things, and the verb agrees with daffodils (plural): which grow.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Although needs a full clause. Before a noun phrase (the heavy rain) use Despite.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: How + adjective + subject + verb: How lovely the moon looks! (What needs a noun: What a lovely moon!)

questions.after: I seen such a bright full moon.
questions.rule: After Never at the start, the helping verb comes before the subject: Never have I seen.
whose shows possession: the poet's poems = the poet whose poems.
Superlative: the most beautiful + noun, often with ever + present perfect.

Look at the sunrise over the hills!
options: What a beautiful sight it is!
How a beautiful sight it is!
questions.rule: What a + adjective + singular noun + subject + verb: What a beautiful sight it is!

questions.source: How sweet the song of the birds is!
options: The song of the birds was very sweet.
The song of the birds are very sweet.
The song of the birds is very sweet.
questions.rule: Replace How with very, keep the same tense (is) and end with a full stop.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: which refers to plural flowers, so grow; the story is in the past (saw), so who loved.

options: Seldom we do see such a clear night sky in the city.
Seldom do we see such a clear night sky in the city.
Seldom do we saw such a clear night sky in the city.
questions.rule: After Seldom at the start: helping verb + subject + base verb: do we see.

options: Although it was cloudy, we enjoyed the trek.
Although it was cloudy, but we enjoyed the trek.
Despite it was cloudy, we enjoyed the trek.
questions.rule: Although takes a clause and does not need but. Despite cannot take a full clause.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: as ... as takes the positive degree: as calm as.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: For a person who does the action, use who: the poet who wrote.

questions.after: peaceful the forest is at dawn!
questions.rule: How + adjective (peaceful) + subject + verb makes an exclamation.
Never first, then helping verb before subject: Never have I seen ...

chat: Aai

Aai
I heard it rained all day.
options: Yes, despite of the rain, we enjoyed it a lot.
Yes, although the rain, we enjoyed it a lot.
Yes, despite the rain, we enjoyed it a lot.
questions.rule: despite + noun, with no of. although needs a full clause.

chat: Sahil
Who is the man near the gate?
options: He is the gardener which looks after our school garden.
He is the gardener who looks after our school garden.
He is the gardener who look after our school garden.
questions.rule: Use who for a person; it refers to the gardener (singular), so looks.

questions.source: Kaas is the most colourful plateau in Maharashtra.
options: Kaas is more colourful than any other plateaus in Maharashtra.
Kaas is more colourful than any other plateau in Maharashtra.
Kaas is most colourful than any other plateau in Maharashtra.
questions.rule: Superlative to comparative: more colourful than any other + singular noun.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: an before a vowel sound (an old tree); which refers to plural trees, so stand.

options: How a sweet dream it was!
What a sweet dream was it!
What a sweet dream it was!
questions.rule: What a + adjective + noun, then subject before verb: it was, not was it.

options: Not only does nature heal us, but it also brings us joy.
Not only nature heals us, but it also brings us joy.
Not only does nature heals us, but it also brings us joy.
questions.rule: Not only at the start needs inversion with a base verb: does nature heal.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The fixed phrase is in spite of + noun.

questions.after: streams stay cool even in May, lies in the Sahyadris.
questions.rule: The streams belong to the village, so use whose + noun.
Double comparative: The more ..., the more ... Both parts need the.
The relative clause that give readers so much joy comes right after poems.

chat: Ananya
How was the view from Sinhagad?
options: Rarely I have enjoyed a view so much!
Rarely have I enjoy a view so much!
Rarely have I enjoyed a view so much!
questions.rule: After Rarely: helping verb + subject + past participle: have I enjoyed.

chat: Dev
Which is cooler, Lonavala or Mumbai?
options: Lonavala is much more cooler than Mumbai.
Lonavala is much coolest than Mumbai.
Lonavala is much cooler than Mumbai.
questions.rule: Two places compared: cooler than. much can strengthen it, but never add more.

questions.source: Although the sky was dark, the children kept playing.
options: In spite of the sky was dark, the children kept playing.
In spite of the dark sky, the children kept playing.
In spite the dark sky, the children kept playing.
questions.rule: In spite of is followed by a noun phrase (the dark sky), not a clause.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Of all needs the superlative the most; the subject is flowers (plural), so make.

options: No sooner had we reached the beach when the sun set.
No sooner did we reached the beach than the sun set.
No sooner had we reached the beach than the sun set.
questions.rule: No sooner + helping verb + subject ... than (not when).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive voice = was + past participle: was built.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A comparative (more peaceful) is followed by than; then means 'after that'.

questions.after: tired, Riya finished painting the sunset.
questions.rule: Despite is a preposition, so a verb after it takes the -ing form: despite being.
No sooner had + subject + past participle ... than + simple past.

chat: Neha
Did you like the poem by Keats?
options: Yes, I did. It is one of the most beautiful poems I have ever read.
Yes, I do. It is one of the most beautiful poems I have ever read.
Yes, I did. It is one of the most beautiful poem I have ever read.
questions.rule: Did you ...? is answered with I did; one of the + superlative + plural noun (poems).

questions.source: The moon is brighter than the stars.
options: The stars are not as brighter as the moon.
The stars are not as bright as the moon.
The stars are not as bright than the moon.
questions.rule: Comparative to positive: not as + positive adjective + as.

questions.source: I have never felt so peaceful.
options: Never I have felt so peaceful.
Never had I felt so peaceful.
Never have I felt so peaceful.
questions.rule: Keep the tense (have felt) and invert: Never have I felt.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: than needs the comparative brighter; in spite of; an before the vowel sound in hour.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Subject John Keats is singular: was; past story: continued; fixed phrase: at the age of.

options: Hardly had the clouds parted than the moon appeared.
Hardly the clouds had parted when the moon appeared.
Hardly had the clouds parted when the moon appeared.
questions.rule: Hardly had + subject + past participle ... when (not than).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Trees are things, so after a preposition use which: under which. whom is only for people.

questions.after: how gloomy the day is, a walk in the garden always lifts my spirits.
questions.rule: No matter how + adjective + clause shows contrast: whatever the situation, the result stays the same.

questions.before: Of the two paths, the river path is
questions.rule: Choosing between two things: the + comparative (the shadier).
How + adverb (gracefully) + subject + verb ... + !

chat: Riya

Riya
Let's stay on the terrace a little longer.
options: Yes, let's. How bright they are!
Yes, let's. How bright are they!
Yes, let's. How bright it are!
questions.rule: In an exclamation the subject comes before the verb: How bright they are!

chat: Kabir
Is this the cafe you told me about?
options: Yes, this is the cafe which we celebrated Riya's birthday.
Yes, this is the cafe where we celebrated Riya's birthday.
Yes, this is the cafe where we celebrate Riya's birthday last year.
questions.rule: For a place where something happened, use where; a past event needs the past tense: celebrated.

questions.source: It is a great joy to watch the sun rise over the sea.
options: What a great joy is it to watch the sun rise over the sea!
What a great joy it is to watch the sun rise over the sea!
How a great joy it is to watch the sun rise over the sea!
questions.rule: What a + adjective + noun + subject + verb: What a great joy it is ...!

questions.source: In spite of the gloomy days, beauty still brings us hope.
options: Although the days are gloomy, beauty still brings us hope.
Although the days are gloomy, but beauty still brings us hope.
Although the gloomy days, beauty still brings us hope.
questions.rule: Although needs a clause (the days are gloomy) and never takes but in the other half.

questions.source: Keats was a Romantic poet. His poems are full of nature.
options: Keats was a Romantic poet whose his poems are full of nature.
Keats was a Romantic poet whom poems are full of nature.
Keats was a Romantic poet whose poems are full of nature.
questions.rule: whose replaces His: do not keep both. whom cannot show possession.
